en: Jātaka:
The Book of Six (Chakkanipāta), Chapter on the Unobstructed (Avāriyavagga)
4. The Neru Jātaka:
“The crows and the flocks of crows, and we who are the best among those that fly—”
We all become equal now,
having come to this mountain.
Here, both lions and tigers—
Jackals and deer— the lowest of beasts—
are all exactly alike;
what indeed is this mountain?
“People know this mountain, Nerū, as the best of peaks;
here dwell those endowed with beauty.”
All living beings dwell there.
Where there may be no honoring,
or where there is the disparagement of the virtuous;
Nor where there is contempt for the lowly;
one should not dwell in such a place.
But where both the indolent and the skillful [are honored], [there one may dwell].
Both the brave and the cowardly are honored there;
the virtuous do not dwell among men who make no distinction between them.
This *neru* does not differentiate between the inferior, superior, and middling;
the *neru* makes no distinction.
"Come, let us depart from Nerañjara.
Thus ends the fourth Jātaka, the Nerañjarā-jātaka.
